chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salmah ibn al-Khattab and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Ali ibn Atiyya al-Zayyat, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the stars (astrology), is it true?' So he (peace be upon him) said; 'Yes. Allah (Exalted and Mighty) sent Jupiter to the earth in the image of a man. So he took a man from the non-Arabs and taught him the stars until he thought that he had mastered it. Then he said to him, 'Look around. Where is Jupiter?' So he said, 'I cannot see it in the sky and I do not know where it is'.

He (peace be upon him) said; 'He left him and grabbed the hand of a man from India. So he taught him until he thought he had mastered it, and said, 'Look at Jupiter, where is it?' So he said, 'My calculation evidences to me that you are the Jupiter'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He gasped a cry and died, and his people inherited his knowledge, so the knowledge is over there (in India)'.

key_terms.النُّجُومِ: The stars (specifically referring to astrology/astronomy in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of astrology and how was it taught according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this unique narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the validity of astrology by recounting how the planet Jupiter descended in human form to teach the art to a Persian and then an Indian, illustrating the celestial origin of astrological knowledge. This account highlights the Shia scholarly view that astrology is not merely superstition but a science derived from direct celestial influence, with the knowledge subsequently inherited by the descendants of the Indian teacher.
